title: Turkey Chili
ingredients: 4 cans (15 oz each) kidney beans, drained and rinsed
4 cups low-sodium chicken broth, vegetable broth, or water
4 tsp packed dark or light brown sugar
1/2 tsp ground cayenne pepper (optional, to taste)
2 1/2 tsp kosher salt (plus more to taste)
instructions: Brown the turkey: Heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large 6- to 8-quart Dutch oven or stockpot over medium-high heat. Add the 2 lbs ground turkey and cook, breaking it up with a spoon, until fully browned and no pink remains (about 8–10 minutes). If your pot is narrow, do this in two batches to prevent steaming. Transfer browned turkey to a plate and set aside.
Sauté the onions: Add the remaining 1 to 2 tbsp olive oil to the same pot over medium heat. Add the chopped yellow onions and a pinch of salt. Cook until softened and translucent (about 5–7 minutes).

Bloom the paste and spices: Stir in the tomato paste, granulated garlic, chili powder, cumin, brown sugar, oregano, paprika, cinnamon, black pepper, cayenne, and kosher salt. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant and the paste turns a deep rusty red.

Combine liquids and simmer: Return the browned turkey and any accumulated juices to the pot. Pour in the crushed tomatoes and broth. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce heat to low, partially cover, and simmer gently for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add corn, beans and finish: Stir in the drained kidney beans and frozen corn. Simmer uncovered for another 10 minutes until heated through and the chili thickens to your desired consistency.
Adjust flavor: Remove from heat and stir in the 2 teaspoons of apple cider vinegar to brighten the flavors. Taste and adjust kosher salt or cayenne if needed. Serve hot.
notes: Double batch. Yield ~12 cups; serving = 1.5 cups (approx. 360g cooked). Estimated nutrition per serving (1 of 8); sodium varies with broth and salt; sugars mostly natural from tomatoes.
